concepts.title: Metaphysical Conceit and Diction in Donne
concepts.definition: An extended, intellectually rigorous metaphor that correlates physical phenomena with abstract emotional states through vibrant language.
concepts.key_idea: Morning and afternoon shadows reflect the rise, culmination, and deceitful decline of human love.
question_patterns: how does John Donne use the metaphor of shadows to represent love
explain the difference between morning and afternoon shadows in Donne's poem
what message does the speaker convey regarding love staying at its noon point
describe metaphysical elements present in A Lecture Upon the Shadow
Explain Metaphysical Conceit and Diction in Donne with a suitable example.

solution_steps.explain: The physical shadows cast by walking lovers represent disguises and misunderstandings in different stages of love.
Morning shadows represent disguises aimed at deceiving external observers while love grows towards noon.
Past midday, declining love generates new internal shadows that blind the lovers themselves, causing relationship decay.

concepts.title: Temporal Decay versus Eternal Divinity in Milton
concepts.definition: A poetic structure juxtaposing fleeting earthly time with transcendent, timeless divine existence.
concepts.key_idea: Earthly suffering and time are finite, whereas divine bliss and soul immortality overcome mortal decay.
question_patterns: why does Milton address time as envious and leaden-stepping
contrast the earthly realm with the divine eternity in On Time
how does Milton describe Shakespeare's monument in On Shakespeare
explain what constitutes the true tribute to Shakespeare's genius
Explain Temporal Decay versus Eternal Divinity in Milton with a suitable example.

solution_steps.explain: Time is depicted as greedy and self-devouring, consuming only transient, false, and mortal dross.

solution_steps.action: contrast temporal loss with divine gain
solution_steps.explain: Once bad earthly elements are entombed, eternal virtues like Truth, Peace, and Love reign supreme.
In On Shakespeare, live-long monuments built in readers' wonder surpass static stone pyramids.

concepts.title: Contrary States of the Human Soul in Blake
concepts.definition: The dual perspective on human nature depicting innocence as inherent divine goodness and experience as institutionalized corruption.
concepts.key_idea: Virtues of love and mercy exist naturally in innocence but are inverted into social tools of dominance in experience.
question_patterns: compare the depiction of human nature in Songs of Innocence and Songs of Experience
how are mercy pity peace and love personified in The Divine Image
explain the origin of the mystery tree in The Human Abstract
how do positive virtues become distorted within the human brain
Explain Contrary States of the Human Soul in Blake with a suitable example.

solution_steps.explain: The Divine Image equates divine essence with human form through Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love.
The Human Abstract shows that Pity requires poverty and Mercy requires inequality to exist.
Virtues become exploited and distorted into deceitful institutional trees rooted in the human mind.

concepts.title: Romantic Vision and Supernatural Imagery in Coleridge
concepts.definition: A poetic portrayal blending vivid natural landscapes with subconscious trance visions and enchanted elements.
concepts.key_idea: Supernatural art combines creative construction with underlying chaos, wild waters, and ancestral warnings.
question_patterns: how does Coleridge juxtapose contrasting images in Kubla Khan
describe the movement and significance of the sacred river Alph
what does the vision of the Abyssinian maid symbolize
explain how poetic ecstasy and inspiration are depicted
Explain Romantic Vision and Supernatural Imagery in Coleridge with a suitable example.

solution_steps.explain: Coleridge pairs the sunny pleasure dome with cold caves of ice and fertile gardens with measureless caverns.
The river Alph flows through deep romantic chasms and tumult before sinking into a lifeless ocean.
Reviving the Abyssinian maid's song inspires the poet to recreate the dome in air, awakening holy dread.

concepts.title: Transience of Youth vs Nature's Permanence in Yeats
concepts.definition: A reflective thematic contrast between human physical aging and the unwearied vitality of natural creatures.
concepts.key_idea: While the aging poet experiences personal decay, the wild swans remain eternally youthful and passionate.
question_patterns: how does Yeats reflect upon aging in The Wild Swans at Coole
contrast the speaker's state of mind with the unwearied passion of the swans
what do autumn imagery and twilight represent in Yeats's poem
explain the significance of the nineteen years spent watching the swans
Explain Transience of Youth vs Nature's Permanence in Yeats with a suitable example.

solution_steps.explain: Trees in autumn beauty and dry woodland paths mirror the poet's declining life stage.
The poet treads with a sore, heavy heart while the swans paddle unwearied in companionable streams.
The potential departure of swans leaves a poignant lingering reflection on fleeting personal energy.

concepts.title: Temporal Discord and Symbolism in Ramanujan
concepts.definition: The poetic examination of urban desynchronization and political discord disrupted by unexpected violence or natural forces.
concepts.key_idea: Out-of-sync city clocktowers parallel societal friction, which is violently silenced by riots or precise natural events.
question_patterns: what causes the differences in timekeeping among urban clocktowers
how does Ramanujan link clock chime variations to social conflicts
why is nature described as precise during a destructive event
explain the impact of human violence on city landmarks in the poem
Explain Temporal Discord and Symbolism in Ramanujan with a suitable example.

solution_steps.explain: Clock gongs ring out of sync due to alloy imperfections, craft maker errors, and varying spatial distances.
Desynchronized gongs symbolize historical feuds and fragile alliances between religious communities.
Clockworks are rendered silent and eyeless by human bomb blasts or calculated lightning strikes.

concepts.title: Ancestral Nostalgia and Decaying Heritage in Kamala Das
concepts.definition: The exploration of aristocratic pride and emotional conflict over an decaying ancestral home versus modern financial realities.
concepts.key_idea: Class distinction and royal blood memories persist even when the family mansion falls into physical decay.
question_patterns: how is the decaying ancestral home portrayed in Kamala Das's Blood
what contrast does the great-grandmother draw between old blood and new rich blood
why does the speaker feel guilt over failing to rebuild the ancestral house
explain how the theme of class privilege is treated in the poem
Explain Ancestral Nostalgia and Decaying Heritage in Kamala Das with a suitable example.

solution_steps.explain: Cracked moist walls, falling roof tiles, and invading rats represent the inevitable decay of past grandeur.
The grandmother takes pride in pure thin ancient blood, contrasting it with the thick gruel blood of poor or new-rich people.
The poet recognizes the difficulty of acquiring wealth, abandoning the physical house while preserving blood memories.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Calculate the number of poetic feet in a line with {line_syllables} syllables.

solution_template.explain: An iambic foot consists of exactly two syllables.
Divide the line's total syllable count by two to find total poetic feet.
